key_insight: Using internal model representations as the nonconformity signal for conformal prediction yields more reliable, deployment-robust uncertainty estimates for LLM question answering than relying solely on output-level signals like token probabilities.
problem_solved: Output-level uncertainty measures (token probs, entropy, self-consistency) become brittle under calibration–deployment mismatch; conformal prediction is valid but depends on a good nonconformity score — this paper addresses how to design such a score for LLMs to preserve coverage and reliability under shift.
method: Extract intermediate internal representations from the LLM (hidden states, layer activations) for each QA example and derive a representation-based nonconformity score.
Apply conformal prediction calibration using these representation scores to produce predictive sets/abstention decisions with finite-sample coverage guarantees under exchangeability.
Evaluate robustness under calibration–deployment mismatch (domain or distribution shift) to show that representation-based scores maintain coverage while keeping predictive sets concise.
impact: Provides a practical path to more trustworthy LLM uncertainty estimates in real-world deployments, enabling safer abstention and better risk management when models encounter distributional shift.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: output-level signals (token probs) vs representation-level signals (hidden states) with arrows to a conformal calibration block.
Pipeline flowchart: Input question → LLM → extract internal representation → compute nonconformity score → conformal calibration → predictive set / abstain.
Bar/line chart: coverage and average predictive-set size under in-domain vs out-of-domain conditions comparing output-based and representation-based conformal methods.
Icon set: LLM model + shield (robustness), magnifying glass over hidden layer (representation), checklist (coverage guarantees)
paper_title: Beyond Surface Statistics: Robust Conformal Prediction for LLMs via Internal Representations
paper_authors: Yanli Wang, Peng Kuang, Xiaoyu Han, Kaidi Xu, Haohan Wang
